hypotheses.persona: A shift worker (likely in construction, maintenance, or a trade) who works a rotating or variable schedule: early morning shifts (departure ~05:00-05:30, return ~14:30) on some days, and later shifts (departure ~13:30, return ~22:30) on others. The consistent use of work badge, keys, thermos, and hi-vis vest indicates a physical job. The laptop and phone are taken to work on early shifts but left at home on later shifts, suggesting they are used for work communication or documentation only during certain shifts. The pattern across days 0-3 showed early departures (Mon-Wed) and a late departure on Thursday. Friday showed a late shift. Saturday and Sunday show relaxed days at home with meals, phone use, and no work items leaving the home. This is consistent with a weekend off. — The weekend pattern (Saturday and Sunday) shows no work-related items leaving the home; instead, the resident had meals, used the phone on the sofa, and stored the thermos in the cupboard. This confirms a weekend off. The shift worker hypothesis is now extremely strong.
hypotheses.rationale: Day 7 (Monday) shows an early shift: hi-vis vest and thermos at home at 04:45, work badge leaves at 05:05, keys and thermos return at 14:10, then evening relaxation. This exactly matches the early shift pattern seen on previous weekdays (Mon-Wed). The weekend off pattern is also confirmed. No evidence of other residents or alternative schedules.

notes: Day 7 (Monday) confirms the early shift pattern: hi-vis vest and thermos at home at 04:45, work badge leaves at 05:05, keys and thermos return at 14:10. Evening routine: plate at table at 18:31, remote on sofa at 19:22, phone on nightstand and remote on coffee table at 20:52, thermos stored at 21:45. This matches previous early shift days (Mon-Wed). The shift worker hypothesis is now extremely strong (p=0.99). The remote worker hypothesis is effectively ruled out. No evidence of other residents.
